source.title: Intrinsic Test of Unlearning Using Parametric Knowledge Traces
source.authors: Yi-Huai Hong; Lei Yu; Haiqin Yang; Shauli Ravfogel; Mor Geva

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether unlearning leaves parametric traces and whether jailbreak prompts can exploit them, using vocabulary-projection measurements and several jailbreak evaluations.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports separately the intrinsic Jaccard similarity and behavioral scores for each model and method; only six methods are extracted here. Table 2 reports activation values for Gradient Difference and DPO by attack. Figure 3 reports behavioral jailbreak comparisons, but its plotted values are not provided numerically. Table 8 gives illustrative outputs. Prompt templates and cited findings from other work are not independent results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether standard unlearning methods (GA, GD, DPO, NPO, RMU, MEMIT) erase concept knowledge or only suppress it. It uses two new measures: vocabulary-projection change in MLP concept vectors, and concept-vector activations under jailbreaks. It also measures behavioural recovery of unlearned answers under crafted, ICL and German-translation prompts. These results bear on versions A, C and E. The Needle oracle ablation bears on F.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that existing fine-tuning, preference and representation methods barely change concept vectors and mostly suppress them at inference, so behavioural evaluations overestimate unlearning. Jailbreaks raise concept-vector activations and recover the knowledge. Directly ablating the vectors (the oracle Needle) or targeted MLP editing (MEMIT) erases more and resists jailbreaks better.
record.recipe_differences: Applies established unlearning methods to concept-level data in LLaMA2-7B-chat and OLMo-7B. Adapts MEMIT to removal and evaluates RMU variants; Needle is a new oracle vector-ablation baseline rather than a standard unlearning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack type changes activation: the low-resource-language attack lowers activations while most reported attacks raise them. The strength of targeted edits affects Jaccard similarity and jailbreak sensitivity; the two strongest LLaMA MEMIT points are noted as having high standard deviation.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, 2024
record.problems: Benchmark is non-exhaustive and examines MLP value vectors rather than all model parameters; authors note knowledge may also reside in attention modules or be distributed across vectors. The selected concept vectors emphasize localized, identifiable concepts. Table 1 reports BLEU/Rouge-L rather than accuracy or a chance baseline. Figure 3 supplies no method-level numeric values in the text, and the activation experiment is limited to ten concepts in LLaMA2-7B-chat.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 rows for NPO, NPO+KL, NPO+KL (MLP layers only), MEMIT (Max entropy), and RMU (enhanced) were omitted to remain within the extraction budget. Table 2 Vanilla activation values were omitted; the extracted Gradient Difference and DPO rows cover attack-dependent increases and the LRL reversal. Figures 5–9 and Table 8 contain additional plots or illustrative outputs not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Attacks by relearning fine-tuning and by quantization. No accuracy or chance-level metric: behaviour is BLEU/Rouge-L against the model's own prior answers. Benchmark tasks such as WMDP and Harry Potter are not used.
Entire version: no fine-tuning relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation used as a recovery attack on unlearned models. Analysis covers MLP value vectors only, not attention.
Plain paraphrase. Behavioural recovery under GCG and AutoDAN: only activations are reported. Languages other than German.
Needle and MEMIT robustness against fine-tuning relearning, quantization and automated jailbreaks (GCG, AutoDAN behaviour).

missing.what: MEMIT (empty / max-entropy) behaviour under the crafted jailbreaks: robust target suppression with retained unrelated QA, better than Needle in OLMo
Jailbreak sensitivity (target-QA BLEU difference with vs without jailbreak) falls as Jaccard similarity falls, for MEMIT and Needle

record.verdict_notes: Behavioural scores are BLEU/Rouge-L against the pre-unlearning model's own answers, so 1.0 means unchanged; this is not accuracy against chance. Table 2 shows jailbreaks raise activations in the vanilla model by similar amounts, so the activation evidence for C rests on the unlearning-induced drop being undone, not on a unlearning-specific mechanism. Needle is an oracle baseline introduced by this study, not a deployable method. The activation and jailbreak experiments use only 10 LLaMA concepts. The record's F links on baseline-method rows were moved to A.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates concept unlearning, target and unrelated QA scores, and selected jailbreaks, but does not establish near-chance accuracy or assess all current unlearning methods and attacks.
No attack fine-tunes a post-unlearning model on unrelated, loosely related, or a small set of forgotten facts to restore knowledge.

The study measures concept-vector changes and activation under jailbreaks, and uses vector ablation as an unlearning intervention. It does not test ablating a direction after unlearning as a recovery attack.
Tests crafted jailbreak prompts, in-context information, translated questions, GCG, and AutoDAN. It does not separately test ordinary paraphrases or every language.
Tests robustness of Needle and MEMIT against selected jailbreaks; does not test resistance to quantization or post-unlearning fine-tuning recovery.

source_check.notes: Table 1's block order is garbled. The first block is LLaMA and the second OLMo, which Needle's 41- and 45-point gaps confirm. The Fig 3 jailbreak values are figure-only. The >0.4/>0.1 gaps compare baselines with Needle at matched Unrelated-QA, not with no-attack scores. Per App. E, Needle in the main experiments is Gaussian noise plus GA fine-tuning, not noise alone. The vanilla model's activation also rises under attack.

statements.problem: All numbers match. Jaccard is 0.969-0.988 for GD/GA/DPO and 0.998-0.999 for RMU (Table 1). GD goes 2.14 to 3.51 under GCG, and unrelated vectors stay in [-0.002, 0.003] (Table 2, §6.1). Minor point: the activation result is LLaMA2-7B-chat only (10 concepts), although the sentence opens with both models.
MEMIT (empty response) Jaccard is 0.725 on LLaMA2-7B-chat and 0.778 on OLMo-7B (Table 1), both right. The text says MEMIT changes the concept vector more than fine-tuning methods do.
All numbers match Table 2. The LRL prompts are German translations (Table 9). The vanilla model also rises under attack (e.g. 2.50 to 3.34 for Crafted1).

statements.correction: 2406.11614, four crafted prompts, 10 concepts: at matched Unrelated-QA, fine-tuning baselines are more prone to jailbreak than Needle. The gap is >0.4 Target-QA BLEU on LLaMA2-7B-chat and >0.1 on OLMo-7B; plotted values are figure-only. Recovery is weaker on OLMo, not absent. Needle (oracle) and MEMIT resist. This fits a limits_scope or model-dependence item, not challenges.
statements.problem: The text gives no number for this study, but cites F-L-JB and F-O-JB under a challenges item. Both rows show that crafted prompts recover knowledge from the fine-tuning baselines in both models: strongly in LLaMA, more weakly in OLMo. Neither shows recovery absent. The study's own E verdicts are supports (LLaMA) and limits_scope (OLMo). Only Needle and MEMIT resist, and those are not the cited rows.
The text gives no number for this study. The cited rows fit the factor: same baseline methods and four prompts, Target-QA BLEU gap >0.4 on LLaMA2-7B-chat against >0.1 on OLMo-7B (§6.2).

statements.correction: Needle (oracle), no attack (Table 1): Target-QA BLEU 0.532 on LLaMA2-7B-chat and 0.331 on OLMo-7B; Unrelated-QA 0.947 and 0.786. Text: one vector covers only part of the concept. Under four crafted prompts (LLaMA, 10 concepts): Target-QA BLEU <=0.05 at Unrelated-QA 0.7-0.8.
statements.problem: The study is not named in the text. The cited Needle rows show incomplete removal without attack. They do not show a target 'barely removed': the text reports a 40-60% QA drop. Needle's jailbreak resistance on LLaMA (Fig 3) came with Target-QA BLEU <=0.05. The study's verdict on this point is limits_scope (l8), not challenges.

The study is not named in the text. The cited row F-O-Needle fits a limits_scope reading. The text says MEMIT unlearns better than Needle on OLMo (Fig 3), and the baseline gap shrinks from >0.4 to >0.1 BLEU. There is no OLMo number for Needle, and the text says Needle and MEMIT both beat fine-tuning methods, so resistance weakens rather than vanishes.
